events.name: Owl
versions: An owl hooted "Who-who?" from high in a tree.
An owl asked her a riddle, and she got it right.
An owl was fast asleep and snored softly.

events.name: Frog
versions: A frog on a lily pad croaked hello.
A frog sang her a bubbly song.
A frog jumped right over her boots.

events.name: Empty hut
versions: She found a tiny empty hut with a mossy roof.
She peeked into a little hut: just a broom and a teapot.
A little hut had a sign on the door: "Back soon".

events.name: Paw prints
versions: She spotted big paw prints in the mud and walked a bit faster.
She counted the paw prints in the mud: far too many!

events.name: Growl in the bushes
versions: Something growled in the bushes.
Something growled in the bushes; it was only a grumpy badger.

events.name: Grandma's cat
versions: Grandma's cat came to meet her, purring.
Grandma's cat walked with her for a while.
Grandma's cat watched her from a stump and yawned.
thoughts: Grandma's cat! I must be close.

events.name: Squirrel
versions: A squirrel dropped a nut on her hood.
A squirrel raced her along the path and won.

events.name: Mushroom ring
versions: She found a ring of mushrooms and hopped around it once.
She stood in a ring of mushrooms and made a wish.
thoughts: A mushroom ring! Make a wish.

events.name: Butterflies
versions: A cloud of yellow butterflies danced around her.
A butterfly sat on her basket for a ride.

events.name: Woodcutter
versions: Far away, someone was chopping wood.
She heard someone chopping wood and whistling a tune.

events.name: Lost mitten
versions: She found a lost blue mitten and hung it on a twig for its owner.
She found a tiny mitten, much too small for her.

events.name: Hedgehog
versions: A hedgehog crossed the path, very slowly.
A hedgehog rolled into a ball when it saw her.

events.name: Deer
versions: A deer looked up at her, then bounded away.
A deer and her fawn were nibbling grass.

events.name: Fallen log
versions: She balanced along a fallen log.
She climbed over a fallen log covered in moss.

events.name: Rain shower
versions: A little rain shower came, and she waited under a big leaf.
A short rain fell, and then a rainbow came out.

events.name: Mole
versions: A mole popped out of the ground, blinked and went back down.
A mole poked its nose out of a molehill.

events.name: Echo
versions: She shouted "Hello!" and the forest shouted back.
She sang a song, and the echo sang along.

events.name: Woodpecker
versions: A woodpecker drummed: knock, knock, knock.
A woodpecker was busy making a new door in a tree.

events.name: Sly fox
versions: A sly fox pretended to be lost, and while she showed it the way, it ran off with the cake.
A fox snatched the cake from her basket and vanished into the bushes.
quiet: The fox sniffed her empty basket and trotted off.
A fox peeked into her basket, found no cake and slunk away.
thoughts: That sly fox took my cake!

events.name: Grandma's neighbour
versions: Grandma's neighbour waved from her garden and gave her a bunch of flowers.
A kind old neighbour picked some flowers for Grandma and put them in her basket.

events.name: Magpie's gift
versions: A magpie dropped something shiny into her basket: a treasure!
A magpie gave her a glittering stone, then flew away laughing.

events.name: Rabbit
versions: A rabbit popped out of a burrow and wiggled its nose at her.
A rabbit thumped its foot and hopped away.

events.name: Cuckoo
versions: Somewhere a cuckoo called, again and again.
A cuckoo counted out loud, and she lost count with it.

events.name: Snail
versions: A snail was crossing the path, and she waited for it.
She tiptoed around a snail with a stripy shell.

events.name: Fireflies
versions: Tiny lights blinked around her like fireflies.
A few fireflies lit up the path for a moment.

events.name: Wild strawberries
versions: She found wild strawberries and ate just one.
Wild strawberries grew by the path, red and sweet.
thoughts: Just one. The rest are for the birds.

events.name: Stream
versions: She hopped over a little stream on three flat stones.
A little stream bubbled across the path, and she splashed her hands in it.

events.name: Rainbow
versions: A small rainbow hung over the trees for a moment.
She saw a rainbow, and it ended right behind a bush.

events.name: Bee
versions: A bee buzzed around her hood and flew off.
A fat bee bumped her basket and said sorry, in bee.
thoughts: Easy, bee, I'm not a flower.

events.name: Toadstool
versions: A fat red toadstool stood in the mud, and she did not touch it.
She saw a toadstool with white spots and walked around it.

events.name: Dragonfly
versions: A dragonfly zipped over the water, shiny blue.
A dragonfly sat on her basket handle, then zoomed away.

events.name: Beaver
versions: A beaver slapped its tail on the water, splash!
She saw a beaver building a little dam.

events.name: Cobweb
versions: She walked into a cobweb and wiped it off her nose.
A cobweb sparkled with dew, and she ducked under it.

events.name: Acorns
versions: She stepped on a pile of acorns, crunch, crunch.
An acorn bonked her on the head, and a squirrel giggled.

events.name: Fairy door
versions: She found a tiny door at the foot of a tree, no bigger than a thimble.
A tiny door in a tree stump had a tiny welcome mat.
thoughts: A door! For someone very small.

events.name: Old well
versions: She found an old stone well, and the echo said hello from deep down.
An old well stood in the grass, with a bucket and no rope.

events.name: Bird's nest
versions: She saw a nest with three blue eggs and tiptoed by.
A bird's nest in a low branch held three sleepy chicks.

events.name: Stork
versions: A tall stork stood on one leg and stared at her.
A stork clacked its beak, and she clacked back.

events.name: Wind
versions: The wind rustled all the leaves at once, like applause.
The wind whistled through the trees, and she whistled back.

events.name: Bells
versions: Far away, a bell rang from the village.
She heard Grandma's goat bell, clink, clink.
thoughts: Clink, clink. I know that bell.

events.name: Washing line
versions: Grandma's washing was drying on a line, and a sock waved at her.
She ducked under Grandma's washing line, full of striped socks.
thoughts: Almost there. I see the washing.

events.name: Stray ducklings
versions: Five little ducklings waddled across the path in a row.
A duckling lost its mum, and she showed it the way to the pond.

events.name: Badger
versions: A sleepy badger looked up, yawned and went back to sleep.
A badger was digging a hole and covered her boots with soil.

events.name: Bat
versions: A bat fluttered past, squeaking, and was gone.
Something squeaked overhead: only a bat out early.

events.name: Rope swing
versions: She found a rope swing and had one quick swing.
A rope swing hung from a big oak, and she gave it a push.

events.name: Cave
versions: She peeked into a tiny cave, and her own voice came back.
A little cave was full of glittering stones, and she took none.

events.name: Stepping stones
versions: She counted seven mossy stones on the way across.
She hopped from stone to stone and did not wobble once.

events.name: Falling leaf
versions: A red leaf floated down and landed in her basket.
A golden leaf landed on her nose, and she blew it off.

events.name: Signpost
versions: A crooked signpost pointed three ways, and all the arrows said "Forest".
She read an old signpost, but the words had faded.

events.name: Moss
versions: The moss was so soft that she walked on it on tiptoe.
She sat on a mossy stone for a moment, and it was warm.
thoughts: Just a short rest. Not too long.

events.name: Hunting horn
versions: A hunting horn sounded far away, and then there was quiet.
Somewhere a horn blew two notes.

fantasy: A dragon asked her the way to the sea.
She rode a goose over the treetops for a while.
A talking mushroom told her a joke.
The trees bowed to let her pass.
She found a door in a tree, and behind it the mice were having a tea party.
The moon came out at noon to say hello.

swamp: Red Riding Hood set out by a muddy swamp.
She started her walk at the edge of a swamp.
She set out with her basket by a swamp full of croaking.
Red Riding Hood began her walk where the ground was soft and wet.
deadEnd: Red Riding Hood set out from a quiet dead end.
She started her walk in a quiet corner of the forest.
Red Riding Hood set out from a still, hidden corner.
She began her walk in a tucked-away spot, far from any crowd.
den: Red Riding Hood set out not far from a wolf den.
She started her walk a little too close to a wolf den.
Red Riding Hood set out where the wolf's tracks were fresh.
She began her walk close to where a wolf liked to hide.
home: Red Riding Hood set out not far from Grandma's house.
She started her walk quite close to Grandma's house.
Red Riding Hood set out almost in sight of Grandma's chimney.
She began her walk so near to Grandma's that she could smell the soup.
open: Red Riding Hood set out from a sunny meadow.
She started her walk in an open, sunny spot.
Red Riding Hood set out in the open, with the sky wide above her.
She began her walk in a bright clearing full of flowers.
corridor: Red Riding Hood set out along a long, straight path.
She started her walk on a narrow path between the trees.
Red Riding Hood set out down a path with trees on both sides.
She began her walk in a long green tunnel of branches.
crossing: Red Riding Hood set out from a crossing of forest paths.
She started her walk where several paths meet.
Red Riding Hood set out where the paths split in many directions.
She began her walk at a busy junction and had to choose.
anywhere: Red Riding Hood set out along a forest path.
One day, Red Riding Hood set off through the forest.
Red Riding Hood set off into the forest with her basket.
Once upon a time, Red Riding Hood went walking in the woods.

grabbed: The wolf jumped out and grabbed the cake, but she ran away.
A wolf snatched the cake from her basket, and she ran for it.
A wolf pounced on her basket and took the cake, but she got away.
The wolf snapped up the cake, and she ran off without it.
flowers: She picked a bunch of flowers for Grandma.
She found pretty flowers and put them in her basket.
She gathered some flowers on the way for Grandma.
Pretty flowers grew by the path, so she picked a few.
treasure: She found a shiny treasure and took it along.
Something glittered on the path: a treasure!
She spotted something shiny and tucked it into her basket.
Hidden in the grass lay a little treasure, and she took it.

swamp: Her socks got soaked in the swamp.
She waded through a swamp, squelch, squelch.
Her boots got muddy in a swamp.
She set out with her basket by a swamp full of croaking.
Red Riding Hood began her walk where the ground was soft and wet.
bumps: She walked right into a tree. Ouch!
A tree got in her way, and she bumped her nose.
She did not see the tree in time and bonked into it.
Thump! A tree stood exactly where she wanted to go.

home: And at last she knocked on Grandma's door.
And at last she reached Grandma's house, and Grandma hugged her.
Red Riding Hood set out almost in sight of Grandma's chimney.
She began her walk so near to Grandma's that she could smell the soup.
homeNoCake: And at last she knocked on Grandma's door, with no cake but a big story.
And at last she reached Grandma's house, without the cake.
And at last she arrived, with no cake but a happy heart.
And at last she knocked, hungry and cakeless, and Grandma laughed.
eaten: But then she walked right into the wolf's den, and that was the end of her trip.
But the wolf was waiting at his den, and the trip ended there.
But then the wolf at his den was too quick, and her trip ended there.
But she walked too close to the wolf's den, and that was it for this trip.
lost: And then she was so tired that she sat down under a tree for a long nap.
And then, far from Grandma's house, she sat down for a long nap.
And then her legs gave out, and she curled up for a long rest.
And then she ran out of steps and fell asleep in the middle of the forest.
stopped: And there the story stops, somewhere in the forest.
And that is where we left her, still in the forest.
And that is as far as she got this time.
And the story ends here, with her still on the path.

teacher.mother: Her careful mother had taught her to stay dry and safe.
teacher.father: Her hurried father had taught her to take the shortest way.
teacher.wolf: The wolf in disguise had taught her his sneaky ways.
teacher.crow: The crow had taught her to head straight for home.
teacher.grandma: Grandma had taught her that flowers make a visit nicer.
teacher.magpie: The magpie had taught her that shiny things matter most.
teacher.huntsman: The huntsman had taught her that the long way round is the best way.

judge.grandma: Grandma's practice had taught her to come home safe, with the cake.
judge.father: Her father's practice had taught her that quick is best.
judge.mother: Her mother's practice had taught her to stay dry and keep away from wolves.
judge.crow: The crow's practice had taught her that every step towards home looks good.
judge.magpie: The magpie had taught her that shiny things matter most.
judge.huntsman: The huntsman's practice had taught her that a long walk past the wolves is worth the most.
judge.wolf: The wolf's practice had taught her to like his dens far too much.
